prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "Choose how you want to bring your new companion to life on your desktop."]
1: ["Pick Your Companion", "Select your favorite preset pet companion to get started quickly."]
2: ["Your Desktop Pet is Ready!", "Review how to interact with, move, and control your new companion.", "Right-click your pet on the desktop anytime to access quick settings."]
3: ["Preparing desktop render engine..."]
4: ["Sign in with your primary account to ensure your saved pets and sync settings stay safe."]
5: ["Use a well-lit photo with a clear background for best custom pet generation results.", "Upload Custom Pet Photo"]
6: ["We will notify you on your desktop as soon as your companion spawns."]
7: ["Select Your Adoption Journey", "Adopt a ready-to-play preset pet or generate your own custom companion."]
8: ["Complete your official adoption certificate to claim your exclusive companion badge!", "Official Pet Owner Badge"]
9: ["Sign In to Save Your Pets", "Connect your account to save your companion across all your desktop devices."]

verdicts.problem: Promises an exclusive reward/free extra and implies collecting personal information via an adoption certificate.
